seo.title: Antarctica Express Air-Cruise by Antarctica21: 6 Days
seo.description: Antarctica21's introductory trip: sail from Ushuaia past Cape Horn and across the Drake, land in the South Shetlands, then fly back to Punta Arenas. Six days, November and March.

tagline: Six days: Cape Horn, the Drake by sea, and a flight home.
answer: The Antarctica Express Air-Cruise is Antarctica21's six-day, five-night introduction to Antarctica. On the regular route guests board in Ushuaia, sail the Beagle Channel to Cape Horn and across the Drake Passage to the South Shetland Islands, then fly from King George Island to Punta Arenas. A reverse route flies south first. It runs in November and March.
overview: The one air-cruise that sails the Drake Passage. Antarctica21 positions it as an introductory option: two days crossing with lectures and seabirds, one day in the South Shetland Islands with a first penguin landing, then the flight north.

faqs: Does the Antarctica Express cross the Drake Passage by sea?
Yes, one way. The regular route sails from Ushuaia across the Drake and flies back; the reverse route flies south and sails north.
Six days and five nights, with one day in the South Shetland Islands.
What if the return flight cannot go?
The ship keeps cruising until the flight is cleared. Antarctica21 states that no refund applies on itineraries that start in Ushuaia.
How much luggage can I take on the flight?

25 kg (55 lb) per person in total, hand luggage included, with no single item over 20 kg. Extra allowance cannot be bought. On the Classic and Polar Circle air-cruises, excess luggage is held in Punta Arenas until you return.
